title: Introduce interleaved metric mapper and token-context snapper for low-latency cost reconstruction
author: Aisha Kapoor
description: Adds an interleaved metric mapping service (metric-joiner) and a lightweight token-context snapper service to enable low-latency reconstruction of token-level cost and latency attribution. Motivation: customers have asked for fine-grained cost/latency signals without paying the storage or ingestion costs of full trace retention. The mapper performs adaptive joins between aggregated metrics and sparse sampled traces, emitting stitched events that can be queried for per-token attribution. The snapper component captures compact token-context snapshots (prefix length, model variant, quantization flags, route metadata) for sampled invocations and stores them in a sharded TTL cache with write-behind export to object storage for longer retention. Key changes: 1) new service metric-joiner/service.go with adaptive windowing and cardinality guard, 2) snapper service with protobuf schema and a fast LRU+reservoir sampler, 3) dashboard JSON for Token Context Timeline and Cost Stitch Explorer, 4) runbook for alert tuning and rollout notes, 5) unit and integration tests for end-to-end stitching. Implementation notes: mapped joins use time-bucketed signatures rather than full trace ids to avoid PII exposure; the snapper redacts prompt text and only stores hash+metadata; runtime exposes a per-tenant sampling knob and a cost-weighted reservoir sampler to bias toward high-cost invocations. Rollout plan: staged rollout to Canary -> Dedicated -> Hosted; default sampling at 0.1% for Hosted controlled via feature flag. Backwards compatibility: endpoints are additive; consumers can opt-in to stitched events. Risks: initial spike in metric cardinality during warmup; mitigations include on-the-fly downsampling and soft-fuse circuit. See linked Linear ENG-4381 and SUP-2078 for incident context.

review_comments: Miguel Santos (2026-02-16): Can we avoid a full table join by using the time-bucketed signature approach you described? Concerned about tenant cardinality.
Aisha Kapoor (2026-02-16): Yes — joiner uses 128-bit signature derived from (tenant, route, prefix-hash, bucket) with HMAC keyed by service KMS. Updated joiner_pipeline.go to reflect this.
Riley Chen (2026-02-17): Snapshot TTL and export cadence look reasonable but add a manual purge endpoint for emergency deletions.
Aisha Kapoor (2026-02-17): Added purge endpoint and documented the access control (audit logged).
Priya Narayanan (2026-02-18): Unit tests are good. Integration test flaky on CI (TestJoinPipelineHighCardinality) — looks like timing assumptions.
Aisha Kapoor (2026-02-18): Tightened the test deterministic clocks and added a backoff in pipeline; reran CI.
Riley Chen (2026-02-19): Approving for canary rollout. Left a suggestion to gate default sampling rate behind feature flag.
Miguel Santos (2026-02-19): Approved after verifying metrics cardinality dashboard during local smoke tests.
ci_summary: CI matrix: build (pass), unit-tests (pass), integration-snapper (initial fail TestJoinPipelineHighCardinality) then rerun pass, lint (pass), e2e-canary (pass). Flaky test fixed by deterministic clock and backoff tweaks.
release_notes: Introduce metric-joiner and token-context snapper. Exposes new stitched events for low-latency per-token cost/latency attribution. Dashboard Token Context Timeline added. Opt-in via feature flag; default Hosted sampling 0.1%. See docs/observability/runbooks/token-snapper-rollout.md for rollout/alert guidance.
runbook_notes: Short runbook: 1) If metric cardinality spikes, toggle feature flag to reduce sampling, 2) Check joiner high_watermark metric and apply automatic downsample circuit, 3) Use purge endpoint to remove snapshots for a tenant (requires SRE approval), 4) Dashboard panels: Cost Stitch Rate, Snapshot Cache Hit, Joiner Dropped Signatures.
backfill_plan: No backfill required for stitched events; a small migration job converts last 48h of sampled snapshots (opt-in) for early Canaries; longer backfill discouraged.
post_merge_steps: Trigger feature-flag rollout to canary tier
Monitor joiner.cardinality and snapshot.cache_hit rate for 48h
Run migration job for opt-in canaries if requested
